meta.title: Terence McKenna, 1946-2000: a working chronology
meta.description: A reconstruction scaffold for the archive project. Seeded from public sources in August 2026; every entry carries its sources and an honest confidence label. Corrections expected and welcome.

conventions.note: An entry with precision 'year' and confidence 'reported' is good practice here. A fabricated exact date is the one unforgivable failure. Where sources conflict, the entry says so and is marked 'disputed'.

entries.title: Terence Kemp McKenna born in Paonia, Colorado
entries.summary: Terence Kemp McKenna is born in the small town of Paonia on Colorado's Western Slope.

entries.title: Dennis McKenna born
entries.summary: His brother and lifelong collaborator Dennis Jon McKenna is born, also in Paonia.

entries.title: Life magazine publishes "Seeking the Magic Mushroom"
entries.summary: Life runs R. Gordon Wasson's account of a Mexican mushroom ceremony. The article, which McKenna encountered as a boy in Paonia, was his first exposure to psilocybin mushrooms.

entries.title: Reads Jung's Psychology and Alchemy
entries.summary: Around age fourteen he reads Carl Jung's Psychology and Alchemy, an early step into the esoteric reading that later filled his lectures.

entries.title: Sent to California at sixteen
entries.summary: He moves to Los Altos, California, to live with family friends, and finishes high school in Lancaster.

entries.title: Encounters the psychedelic literature
entries.summary: Through Aldous Huxley's books and The Village Voice he meets the psychedelic writing of the day.

entries.title: Enrolls at UC Berkeley
entries.summary: McKenna begins undergraduate study at the University of California, Berkeley.

entries.title: Accepted into the Tussman Experimental College
entries.summary: He is admitted to Berkeley's Tussman Experimental College, a two-year interdisciplinary program that let him shape his own course of study.

entries.title: First DMT experience
entries.summary: Introduced by Rick Watson, he smokes DMT for the first time, an experience he described for the rest of his life. In the same period he begins studying Tibetan religion.

entries.title: Travels to Jerusalem; meets Kathleen Harrison
entries.summary: On a trip to Jerusalem he meets Kathleen Harrison, the ethnobotanist he would later marry.

entries.title: Travels to Nepal
entries.summary: He goes to Nepal in pursuit of Tibetan painting and shamanic tradition, part of several years of travel through Asia.

entries.title: Customs seizure ends a smuggling sideline
entries.summary: One of his hashish shipments is seized by US customs. He spends the following period moving through Southeast Asia and Indonesia, partly earning his way collecting butterflies.

entries.title: The butterfly collection
entries.summary: McKenna collects butterflies in Indonesia and elsewhere, wrapping specimens in scrap paper of the period. The surviving collection later became the material for his daughter Klea's 2008 book.

entries.title: Death of his mother
entries.summary: Hazelle McKenna dies of cancer. Both brothers later tied the timing of the Amazon expedition to this loss.

sources.label: Reality Sandwich: The Experiment at La Chorrera

entries.title: Expedition sets out for La Chorrera
entries.summary: Terence, Dennis, and three companions travel into the Colombian Amazon toward La Chorrera, a mission settlement on the Rio Igara Parana. The stated goal was oo-koo-he, a DMT snuff; what they found was Psilocybe cubensis.

sources.label: Attar Media: McKenna Explores the Invisible Landscape
Reality Sandwich: The Experiment at La Chorrera

entries.title: Arrival at La Chorrera
entries.summary: The party reaches La Chorrera in late February. Sources agree on the month; this project has not yet pinned the exact day to a primary document.

sources.label: Attar Media: McKenna Explores the Invisible Landscape
Reality Sandwich: The Experiment at La Chorrera

entries.title: The experiment at La Chorrera
entries.summary: On the evening of March 4 the brothers attempt Dennis's protocol combining psilocybin mushrooms and harmine, intending nothing less than a permanent physical change in reality. Dennis's memoir dates the session precisely.

sources.label: Reality Sandwich: The Experiment at La Chorrera
Attar Media: McKenna Explores the Invisible Landscape

entries.title: The two weeks after the experiment
entries.summary: Dennis passes through roughly two weeks of severe psychological disturbance while Terence, watching over him, begins the speculations about time and the I Ching that became the timewave.

sources.label: Reality Sandwich: The Experiment at La Chorrera
Attar Media: McKenna Explores the Invisible Landscape

entries.title: Return from the Amazon
entries.summary: The group leaves La Chorrera and the brothers eventually return to the United States. Accounts differ on how quickly they left: one has them flying to Bogota within days of the experiment, others describe a longer stay.

sources.label: Attar Media: McKenna Explores the Invisible Landscape
Reality Sandwich: The Experiment at La Chorrera

entries.title: The timewave idea is seeded
entries.summary: Out of the La Chorrera experience Terence begins constructing a mathematical map of novelty from the King Wen sequence of the I Ching. The idea occupied him for the rest of his life.

entries.title: Returns to Berkeley
entries.summary: He goes back to UC Berkeley to finish his interrupted studies.

entries.title: First computed timewave: FORTRAN on a CDC 6400
entries.summary: Royce Kelley and Leon Taylor compute the wave's values in FORTRAN on a CDC 6400 at Berkeley, producing the 64 tables of 384 terms behind the original Kelley number set.

entries.title: Graduates from Berkeley
entries.summary: McKenna takes his degree in ecology, shamanism, and natural resource conservation, a self-shaped course of study in the Tussman spirit.

entries.title: The Invisible Landscape published
entries.summary: The Invisible Landscape: Mind, Hallucinogens and the I Ching (Seabury Press), written with Dennis, publishes the La Chorrera speculations and the first form of the timewave. The first edition circulated narrowly.

entries.title: Marries Kathleen Harrison
entries.summary: He marries the ethnobotanist Kathleen Harrison, in the autumn of 1975 according to the Wikipedia account. A primary record has not yet been checked.

entries.title: Psilocybin: Magic Mushroom Grower's Guide
entries.summary: The brothers publish their cultivation manual with And/Or Press under the pseudonyms O. T. Oss and O. N. Oeric. Their method made home cultivation of Psilocybe cubensis practical for the first time.

entries.title: Birth of Finn and Klea
entries.summary: Terence and Kathleen's two children, son Finn and daughter Klea, are born in this period. The project still needs a family statement or record for exact dates.

entries.title: First graphical timewave software
entries.summary: Peter Broadwell's BASIC program for the Apple II+ gives the timewave its first on-screen graph.

entries.title: Independent Pascal implementation in Germany
entries.summary: Klaus Scharff writes an independent Pascal version of the timewave software, evidence of the theory's early spread beyond McKenna's own circle.

entries.title: Becomes a public lecturer
entries.summary: In the early 1980s McKenna emerges as a speaker on the California circuit, the start of nearly two decades of recorded talks. Session-level dating of the early years is thin.

entries.title: "Tryptamine Hallucinogen Consciousness" at Esalen
entries.summary: Recorded at the Esalen Institute in December 1982, this is the earliest Esalen lecture the institute has republished from its own archive.

entries.title: The Esalen years
entries.summary: By Esalen's own count McKenna taught there nearly one hundred times, with seminars such as Dynamics of Hyperspace and Our Cyberspiritual Future. Dating each visit from Esalen's records is a major open task for this chronology.

entries.title: Dennis McKenna earns his doctorate
entries.summary: Dennis completes a PhD in botanical sciences at the University of British Columbia, on the pharmacology of Amazonian hallucinogenic plants. The brothers' paths diverge: one into science, one onto the stage.

entries.title: Peter Meyer meets McKenna
entries.summary: Programmer Peter J. Meyer meets McKenna. Their collaboration produced every later edition of the timewave software.

entries.title: Botanical Dimensions founded
entries.summary: Terence and Kathleen found Botanical Dimensions, a nonprofit for preserving ethnobotanically significant plants and the knowledge around them, anchored by a forest garden on the Big Island of Hawaii.

entries.title: Revised mushroom guide
entries.summary: A revised edition of the grower's guide appears; combined sales passed one hundred thousand copies.

entries.title: Meyer's Apple //e timewave software
entries.summary: Meyer writes the Apple //e version of the software, visiting McKenna in Hawaii in 1987 to work on it. Watkins' account credits Meyer with introducing the wave's full fractal nesting in this period.

entries.title: Timewave Zero software (contested dating)
entries.summary: Wikipedia dates the completed Timewave Zero software, by Meyer in collaboration with McKenna, to July 1987. The restoration dossier instead places the Apple //e work in 1986 and 1987 and the MS-DOS program named Timewave Zero in 1989 to 1991. The year is kept and the conflict flagged.

entries.title: First public trialogue, Esalen
entries.summary: McKenna, Rupert Sheldrake, and Ralph Abraham hold their first public three-way conversation at Esalen. The institute's archive preserves the recording with an exact date.

entries.title: First trialogue series at Esalen
entries.summary: The 1989 series with Sheldrake and Abraham ranges over light and vision, the unconscious, the resacralization of the world, and the apocalypse. The three had been talking privately since meeting in 1982.

entries.title: Timewave Zero for MS-DOS
entries.summary: Meyer rewrites the software in C for MS-DOS under the name Timewave Zero and extends its range to 4.5 billion years. In December 1990 the program's default zero date becomes December 21, 2012.

entries.title: The zero date settles on December 21, 2012
entries.summary: Watkins reports that McKenna first reached mid-November 2012 by adding 67.28 years to Hiroshima, then shifted to the winter solstice after learning it ended the Maya calendar. Accounts of exactly when and why the date moved do not agree.

entries.title: "This Is the Mushroom's Program"
entries.summary: A February 1991 talk on the etiquette of working with plant teachers, preserved by the Psychedelic Salon as episode 484. The venue is not recorded in the program notes.

entries.title: Second trialogue series at Esalen
entries.summary: The 1991 sessions take up saving the world, gender, cannabis, crop circles, and psychedelics and the computer revolution.

entries.title: The Archaic Revival
entries.summary: A collection of essays and interviews from 1983 to 1990. Open Library records the HarperOne paperback of May 1992; some references cite a 1991 first edition, so the month is left open here.

entries.title: Food of the Gods
entries.summary: Food of the Gods: The Search for the Original Tree of Knowledge (Bantam) argues that psilocybin mushrooms shaped early human cognition. Ethnobotanist Richard Evans Schultes reviewed it warmly; it remains his most systematic book.

entries.title: Synesthesia
entries.summary: A limited-edition artist book collaboration published the same year as Food of the Gods.

entries.title: Trialogues at the Edge of the West
entries.summary: Bear and Company publishes the first trialogue book with Sheldrake and Abraham, later retitled Chaos, Creativity and Cosmic Consciousness.

entries.title: Boss Drum carries McKenna onto the pop charts
entries.summary: The Shamen's platinum album Boss Drum (One Little Indian) includes Re:Evolution, eight minutes of McKenna spoken word over the band's production.

entries.title: Retires from Botanical Dimensions; divorce
entries.summary: Terence retires from Botanical Dimensions, and he and Kathleen divorce the same year. Kathleen has directed the organization ever since.

entries.title: Third trialogue series at Esalen
entries.summary: The 1992 sessions cover psychedelics and mathematical vision, the immediate future and the millennium, and utopianism.

entries.title: "Re:Evolution" released as a single
entries.summary: The Shamen release Re:Evolution as a single, putting McKenna's voice into the UK charts and in front of the rave generation.

entries.title: True Hallucinations
entries.summary: True Hallucinations (HarperSanFrancisco) finally tells the La Chorrera story at book length, twenty-two years after the events it recounts.

entries.title: The Invisible Landscape, revised edition
entries.summary: HarperSanFrancisco reissues The Invisible Landscape with Peter Meyer's appendix on the mathematics of the timewave. Watkins' account gives 1994 for the republication and the dossier gives 1993; worth settling from the copyright page.

entries.title: Trialogues at Hazelwood, Devon
entries.summary: The trialogues travel to England: homing pigeons, time, fractal boundaries, angels and entities.

entries.title: Meyer's WEN_SRCH and WEN_GRPH tools
entries.summary: Meyer builds tools that generate 384-value sets from any hexagram ordering, not just King Wen. They later mattered for testing how special the original sequence really is.

entries.title: Trialogues at McKenna's Hawaii home
entries.summary: Sheldrake and Abraham record with McKenna at his home in Hawaii, including two sessions on the World Wide Web, then a novelty.

entries.title: Speaks at the Starwood Festival
entries.summary: McKenna appears as a speaker at the Starwood Festival. The Wikipedia article notes the year without a program-level date.

entries.title: Essay in New Statesman and Society
entries.summary: He publishes an essay in the British weekly New Statesman and Society.

entries.title: "Hacking Reality" talk
entries.summary: A talk recorded in October 1995 and circulated by the Psychedelic Salon as episode 702, comparing cultures to computer operating systems. Venue unrecorded.

entries.title: Meets Matthew Watkins at Palenque
entries.summary: At an entheobotany gathering at the Maya site of Palenque, Mexico, McKenna meets the mathematician Matthew Watkins, who had been corresponding with him about flaws in the timewave. Fourmilab's copy of the resulting paper places the meeting in January 1996; Watkins' later account says spring.

entries.title: The Watkins Objection published
entries.summary: Watkins' paper, Autopsy for a Mathematical Hallucination?, is posted on McKenna's own website with McKenna's introduction. It shows the half twist in the 1975 construction has no mathematical justification. McKenna published the critique of his own theory rather than suppressing it.

entries.title: Sheliak's reconstruction of the wave
entries.summary: Physicist John Sheliak circulates a vector-formalized reconstruction, sometimes called Timewave One, intended to answer the Watkins Objection. The dossier dates the work to 1997 and 1998.

entries.title: Fractal Time software
entries.summary: Meyer's final DOS program, Fractal Time, ships all four historical number sets: Kelley, Watkins, Sheliak, and Huang Ti. Copies of the software survive on the Internet Archive.

sources.label: Internet Archive: TWZ / Fractal Time software

entries.title: The Evolutionary Mind
entries.summary: The second trialogue book with Sheldrake and Abraham is published.

entries.title: Final recorded trialogues
entries.summary: The last trialogue recordings, made at various locations: skepticism, morphogenetic family fields, and a closing question and answer session.

entries.title: Diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme
entries.summary: After increasingly severe headaches McKenna collapses and is diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme, an aggressive brain cancer. Treatment, including experimental procedures, continued over the following months.

entries.title: Hosts the AllChemical Arts Conference, Kona
entries.summary: McKenna hosts a conference on visionary states and creativity in Kona, Hawaii, four months after his diagnosis. For many attendees it was the last time they saw him.

entries.title: Final gathering at Esalen
entries.summary: A last, small gathering at Esalen after brain surgery, released by the Psychedelic Salon in 2025. The program notes do not date the recording; establishing the date is an open task.

entries.title: The Erik Davis interview
entries.summary: In late 1999 McKenna gives a long interview to the writer Erik Davis about his life and his approaching death.

entries.title: Terence McKenna dies
entries.summary: McKenna dies in San Rafael, California, at the age of 53.

entries.title: The Psychedelic Salon begins
entries.summary: Lorenzo Hagerty starts the Psychedelic Salon podcast, which becomes the largest public outlet for McKenna's recorded talks over the following two decades.

entries.title: The library fire
entries.summary: A fire in Monterey, California destroys McKenna's library of over 3,000 rare books and personal papers, held in storage since his death. Dennis preserved an index of the collection. The loss defines much of the archive work that remains.

entries.title: The Butterfly Hunter
entries.summary: Klea McKenna publishes The Butterfly Hunter, photographing her father's 1969 to 1972 butterfly collection with the scrap paper he wrapped it in, in an edition of 480 copies with a previously unpublished McKenna short story.

entries.title: Kickstarter for Dennis's memoir
entries.summary: Dennis McKenna launches a crowdfunding campaign for his memoir of life with Terence.

entries.title: The Brotherhood of the Screaming Abyss
entries.summary: Dennis's memoir (North Star Press) becomes a primary source for the family history and the La Chorrera chronology, including the March 4, 1971 dating used in this timeline.

sources.label: Reality Sandwich: The Experiment at La Chorrera

entries.title: The zero date passes
entries.summary: The timewave's terminus arrives and passes without incident, twelve years after McKenna's death. The theory's public test is part of its record.

entries.title: Original software preserved online
entries.summary: Timewave Zero and Fractal Time binaries are uploaded to the Internet Archive, keeping the original programs downloadable and runnable.

sources.label: Internet Archive: TWZ / Fractal Time software

entries.title: Academic study of La Chorrera
entries.summary: Erik Davis publishes The Weird Naturalism of the Brothers McKenna, an academic treatment of the experiment at La Chorrera, in the International Journal for the Study of New Religions.

sources.label: Techgnosis: The Weird Naturalism of the Brothers McKenna

entries.title: Esalen republishes the 1982 lecture
entries.summary: The Voices of Esalen podcast releases the December 1982 lecture from the institute's own tape archive, with commentary by Allan Badiner. Institutional archives still hold undigitized McKenna material.

entries.title: An unheard recording surfaces
entries.summary: The Psychedelic Salon releases a previously uncirculated recording of McKenna's final Esalen gathering. A quarter century after his death, new tape is still surfacing.

entries.title: Authorized releases announced by the family site
entries.summary: terencemckenna.com, maintained with the family, announces new authorized audio releases for 2026 and describes the decades of unauthorized reproduction the estate is working to correct.

entries.title: The timewave restored as a web instrument
entries.summary: The timewave software is restored for the web, verified digit for digit against Meyer's original program. This chronology is scaffolding for the same restoration effort.
